Arjun: Heads-up — nightly long-context (L=4096) perf run shows a spike in p99 generation latency for the new fused_flash_variant. p50 fine, but p99 ~+30% vs yesterday. NSYS & perfetto attached: https://perfetto.link/trace/abc123 and s3://redwood-perf/nsys/2500001111.nsys

Maya: Which job and commit? any repro harness?

Arjun: job: nightly/long-context-chat-A100, commit: 9f2c4e6 (batch-selector: prefer fused_flash_variant_v2 for >2k tokens). Repro locally with microbench: repros on A100, less clear on H100.

Josh: Can you paste the hot kernel timeline from the nsys capture?

Arjun: Paste from nsys (trimmed):
```
Time(ms)   Kernel                              Calls   GPU Time(ms)
0.00       fused_flash_attn_v2_forward          1       184.3
184.3      kv_cache_write_batch                  16      72.5
256.8      kv_cache_read_batch                   32      96.7
353.5      fused_flash_attn_v1_forward          1       20.1
```
Note: fused_flash_attn_v2 is dominant; lots of KV write/read chattiness right after it.

Rachel: That kv_cache_write_batch looks suspicious — is it synchronous in the runtime now? We switched to flushing writes at end-of-step in the adapter change last week.

Arjun: Right — adapter change (9f2c4e6) altered writeback timing to try to reduce memory pressure. It looks like for long sequences writes are being issued more frequently and serializing with the next attn kernel. nvprof sample shows high L2/store stalls on kv_write kernel:
```
== Null == nvprof: sample: kernel kv_cache_write_batch, SM stalls: 42%, L2 writebacks: 1.9GB/s, avg duration 4.5ms per call
```

Devon: Any evidence of bank conflicts or shared mem serialization?

Arjun: perfetto flame shows repeated small write kernels interleaved with attn. SM utilization drops between flashes. Suspect small writes are preventing warps from overlapping next attn launch. Also saw increased host syncs in runtime log:
```
[2026-02-12T03:12:10Z] batch_selector: picked fused_flash_v2 for request=abc
[2026-02-12T03:12:10Z] kv_cache: flushing writes sync=true size=16
[2026-02-12T03:12:10Z] runtime: launch fused_flash_attn_v2
[2026-02-12T03:12:10Z] runtime: cudaDeviceSynchronize() // unexpected
```

Maya: cudaDeviceSynchronize in hot path would explain p99 tail. Was sync added intentionally?

Arjun: It was added as a defensive fix in adapter to guarantee write visibility before next kernel on some older drivers. But it probably regresses overlapped execution.

Josh: Options: 1) revert sync and add explicit stream ordering with events, 2) coalesce kv writes into fewer larger kernels, 3) change batch-selector thresholds to avoid fused_flash_v2 for >2k until we fix.

Rachel: We should triage quickly: reproduce with nvprof+nsys, add sampling to batch-selector to force routing to v1 vs v2, and run microbench with and without sync. I'll take coalesce experiment.

Devon: I'll run a bisect on the adapter change to confirm it's the culprit. Running 9f2c4e6..HEAD on nightly harness now.

perf-bot: New perf run queued: nightly/long-context-chat-A100 (bisect candidate). Job: perf-2500002222.

Arjun: For repro steps:
- Checkout 9f2c4e6 and HEAD
- Run: `./infra/tools/microbench --model gpt-small --seq_len 4096 --batch 1 --profile nsys --gpus a100-80`
- Capture: `nsys profile -o out.nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx ./run.sh`
- Perfetto capture from CI tarball: https://perfetto.link/trace/abc123

Josh: I instrumented the runtime to dump `kv_cache` op sizes and sync calls. Quick sample: `kv_ops: [write:4, write:1, write:1, read:2, write:8] syncs: [true,false,true]` — small writes sprinkled.

Arjun: Proposed short-term mitigation: flip batch-selector to prefer fused_flash_v1 for requests with >2048 tokens until we implement coalesce or stream-events. Patch on my branch: batch-selector/avoid-spread-9f2c4e6.

Maya: Can we also add a runtime assert that forbids cudaDeviceSynchronize in the hot path unless explicitly gated by env var?

Rachel: Yes — doing that as well. I'll send a PR for coalescing kv writes (group contiguous small writes into one kernel) and a separate PR for removing implicit syncs (use events).

Devon: Bisect results: adapter commit 9f2c4e6 introduces behavior change — confirmed. Reverting sync+changing write schedule restores baseline p99 in local runs.

Arjun: OK owners and next steps:
- Arjun: land batch-selector fallback (short-term)
- Rachel: PR for kv coalescing and event-based ordering (medium-term)
- Maya: runtime assert + test (prevent accidental syncs)
- Devon: follow-up regression tests in nightly harness

Arjun: I'll also schedule a perf run across H100 to see if hardware differences hide/mitigate the overlap problem. For trace analysis follow-ups, I'll attach nvprof counters and a full perfetto timeline to the issue: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4721

perf-bot: perf job perf-2500002222 finished: p99 delta -2% (after selector fallback), full report: https://perf-reports.internal/2500002222

Maya: Nice. Keep notes in the ticket; we'll coordinate a rollback window if the fix causes any regressions in cost/throughput. :thumbsup:

Josh: Closing loop: also check quantized kernels — sometimes fused variant has different memory access patterns under q4/q8 that could amplify write stalls.

Arjun: Agreed. Adding quantized harness next. I'll post updated traces in the ticket when available.
